text:
Aisha: Heads up — we've got a recurring pattern of GPU evictions on several A100-40GB nodes in rack-15 and rack-18 over the past 48h. Symptoms: sudden process exits with Xid 13, ECC corrected spikes, then thermal throttling.
Tom: Can you paste the dmesg snippets and serials?
Aisha: Pasting the latest from node infra-r15-gpu03:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID=23782, GPU=a100-40gb
[ 12345.679000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, EccCounter=312, CorrectedErrorCount=289
[ 12346.001234] thermal_warn: GPU temp spike: sensor0=96C -> throttle
[ 12346.001500] kernel: GPU driver reset due to Xid 13
```
Aisha: Serial prefix common to affected cards: SN-AX7**** (we've seen ~9 cards so far across two racks).
SRE-Bot: Alert — 9 similar Xid 13 events detected in last 24h across cluster tags gpu=a100-40gb. Threshold exceeded. :rotating_light:
Katrina: That serial prefix rings a bell — we had a vendor shipment flagged last quarter with SN-AX7* units. Possibly a bad batch.
Eli: Agree. Early signs point to memory ECC correction flood causing thermal runaway and eventual resets. Can we confirm if ECC corrected counts correlate immediately before the Xids?
Aisha: Yes — counts spike ~30-60s before the Xid. I've attached a CSV (pasted below) of timestamps -> ECC counts for the 3 worst nodes:
```
infra-r15-gpu03,2026-02-18T03:12:21Z,Corrected=289
infra-r18-gpu02,2026-02-18T05:44:10Z,Corrected=274
infra-r15-gpu07,2026-02-19T01:05:33Z,Corrected=301
```
Tom: Any recent firmware/driverversion changes on those hosts? Could be regression.
Aisha: Drivers pinned to 510.73 across fleet. Firmware: HBM v1.2. No recent fleet-wide updates.
NV-Support-Bot: Ticket #NV-8921 opened with vendor. Preliminary response: "AX7 prefix historically associated with early production SKUs; requesting power/thermal telemetry and serial ranges."
Katrina: Plan proposal: 1) Immediately drain the 9 affected GPUs from scheduling. 2) Run vendor-provided memory soak on 2 quarantined nodes to reproduce. 3) RMA affected serials as a batch if vendor confirms manufacturing issue. 4) Roll a non-invasive firmware update candidate to one node if vendor suggests.
Tom: Capacity impact? If we drain 9 A100-40GB GPUs that's ~9 GPUs / 320 total A100s in prod = ~2.8% capacity. We should be able to absorb with autoscale but need to inform customers on the dedicated fleet.
Eli: For reproduction, let's run:
- cuda_memtest --pattern=wand --duration=6h
- stress-ng --gpu 4 --timeout 2h
- collect hwmon, BMC, and power consumption every 5s
Katrina: I'll own the soak tests. ETA: start tonight (UTC) and run 24h.
Aisha: I'll compile the serial list and schedule the drain windows with Tom. Also will collect BMC logs and attach to NV ticket.
Tom: I'll schedule the drains in two waves (rack-15 first, then rack-18) during low traffic window 0300-0500 UTC, prefer rolling one GPU at a time per node.
SRE-Bot: FYI — automatic rollback policy will keep fallback nodes ready. No SLA blips expected based on sim.
Eli: If vendor confirms batch defect, bulk RMA. Also consider setting a temporary power cap profile for the remaining AX7 cards to reduce thermal headroom while replacements are pending. Need to test for perf impact.
Katrina: Good call. I can test power capping on one node: set power_limit to 250W and run perf regressions.
Tom: Communication: Draft customer-safe note for dedicated customers in case the RMA timeline extends >72h. I'll start a short incident advisory if tests reproduce.
Aisha: Evidence list I'm collecting: dmesg, ECC CSV, BMC logs, hwmon time series, node power draw, serial list. Will attach to ticket NV-8921 and ping vendor contact.
NV-Support-Bot: Vendor asks for batch number and photos of label; also requested current BIOS/HBM versions.
Katrina: Next steps recap:
- Aisha: collect artifacts + open vendor RMA batch request (owner)
- Katrina: run soak + power cap perf test (owner)
- Tom: schedule drains + customer comms (owner)
- Eli: coordinate fallback plan + test memstress configs (owner)
Everyone: update this thread with status bits.
Tom: If tests reproduce, we'll escalate to SOC and mark affected cards 'quarantine' in inventory DB so they aren't used in future scheduling.
Aisha: Noted. I'll add a quarantine tag on the serials once drain starts.
Eli: Also adding a Prom alert: gpu.ecc_corrected.rate > 200 in 1m for any node — temporary rule for 72h.
SRE-Bot: Alerting rule added.
Katrina: Thanks team. I'll post results and perf numbers in this thread once the first soak completes (~24h). :thumbsup:
Tom: Thanks — keep updates short here. If vendor asks for access we can coordinate secure upload to their portal.
Aisha: Starting drain wave 1 at 0305 UTC. Quarantine tags will be added as GPUs are offline.
Katrina: Soak started 0310 UTC on infra-r15-gpu03 and infra-r15-gpu07.
Eli: I'll standby for data and can run remote debugging sessions with vendor if needed.
NV-Support-Bot: Vendor acknowledges receipt of artifacts; asked for queue ETA ~48h for RMA triage.
Aisha: Closing loop — first soak showed reproduced CorrectedError spike -> Xid 13 on infra-r15-gpu03 at 07:12 UTC, matching original pattern. RMA looks likely.
Tom: OK moving to RMA batch plan. Will create a postmortem draft after RMA schedule confirmed.
Katrina: Filing follow-up runbook items: add a daily short window for AX7 serial checks until replacements arrive.
Eli: Also recommend adding a small test to nightly canary that runs a quick ECC stress for 30m on a random AX7-tagged GPU.
Aisha: Thank you. Updating NV ticket with reproduction artifacts now.
Tom: Keep this thread for the RCA notes and final postmortem. :eyes:
Katrina: +1
Eli: +1
SRE-Bot: Incident advisory draft created at https://internal.redwood/alerts/8921 (internal)
Aisha: Will post postmortem link after RMA completes.
Tom: Great work, team.
